identity: Maastricht University, University College Venlo, English full-time Liberal Arts and Sciences bachelor focused on sustainable food systems. Distinct from University College Maastricht and Maastricht Science Programme.

sources.scope: 2026–27 MSLAS EER Articles 3.6–3.9, 5.2 and Appendix I, UCV modules. Establishes degree credits, concentration rules, pass/fail Portfolio and compulsory module list.
2026–27 UCV Course Catalogue. Confirms course subjects, module credits, Applied Researcher sequence, fifth-semester 2.5 EC Portfolio and 140 EC Capstone threshold.
Official University College Venlo bachelor identity and sustainable food systems scope.
Official course and curriculum overview. Behaviour, Health and Responsible Innovation are thematic directions within flexible study.
Official programme rationale. Production and consumption, food innovation, nutrition, behaviour and research examples.

curriculum: The single-concentration illustration totals 180 EC. It includes 20 core-course EC, 20 introductory core skills/project EC, 2.5 final-year Portfolio EC, 15 general education EC, 75 concentration-course EC, 12.5 concentration skills EC, 15 concentration project EC and 20 Capstone EC. Article 3.8 gives 20 EC for the combined core skills and projects, while the itemised Appendix and catalogue agree on the 2.5 EC advanced core Portfolio in addition to the 20 EC introductory set. The illustration follows the named entries, explicitly retaining that reporting discrepancy. It does not assert that the three thematic pillars are separate regulatory concentrations. Article 3.8 gives 10–20 EC general education for a single concentration, with at least one humanities and one alternate-domain course, or 10 EC of humanities for interdisciplinary study. Article 3.9 gives 70–80 EC concentration courses, at least 20 advanced across at least three courses and at most 20 introductory. One of three concentration projects must be advanced.
progression: The introductory Applied Researcher I–III sequence develops a proposal, collects data, then analyses results in R and communicates findings in a group article and a poster. Applied Researcher II requires I, and III requires I and II. The advanced Portfolio is pass/fail and is listed from semester 5, with reflections drawn from the three years. The Capstone is a final scholarly project with entry after 140 EC. The separate Food in Transition project applies systems thinking to an interdisciplinary food challenge.

This is the last part of a three-period group research project. Students analyse their data, write an article and present a poster.
Designing Research: Quantitative and Qualitative Approaches
This 2.5 EC pass/fail module is listed in the fifth semester. It records curriculum choices and personal and professional development.
The example uses 15 EC outside a single concentration, including humanities and the alternate concentration. Interdisciplinary curricula instead require 10 EC of humanities.
The example uses 75 EC of concentration courses. The concentration requires at least 20 EC of advanced coursework and allows at most 20 EC of introductory coursework.
